title: Brand new Extension threw an exception: "Missing DB manager" in python
body:
### What happens?

I am trying to start developing my own extension.
I followed the procedure from duckdb extension template: created my own git repo "quack2" from template, cloned, built... no extra code involved yet

Tried ./duckdb -unsigned, 
Installed extension from file, loaded, all ok.

Then all interesting started from trying to load it in python.

On load_extension part getting Segmentation fault (core dumped) , of course hard way, no try and catch in help.

Please look at it please

### To Reproduce

```python
import duckdb
import os

con = duckdb.connect(database=':<nick>:', read_only=False, config={'allow_unsigned_extensions': 'true', 'allow_extensions_metadata_mismatch': 'true'})

try:
    con.execute(f"install 'extension/quack2/quack2.duckdb_extension';")
    con.load_extension('quack2')
    print("Extension loaded successfully.")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Failed to load extension: {e}")
```
### OS:

Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS

### DuckDB Version:

v1.0.0 1f98600c2c

### DuckDB Client:

Python 3.8.10

### Full Name:

Eugene Plaksienko

### Affiliation:

CACI Inc

Linux extensions are build using many-linux images, and it might be possible that buildigng from source in arbitrary environment generates compatible extensions.

I would try to reproduce this using quack / the extension template, and compare what you build locally cloning extension-template + building + loading on Python with the results of what's built by CI.

That it should be doable and somewhat reproducible, and something that becomes viable taking a look at.

Otherwise try have your extension built by CI, and see if that can be loaded in your local Python.

comments.body:
two questions:
- what's the version of your duckdb submodule?
- why are you passing the `allow_extensions_metadata_mismatch` flag? this indicates that you are building for the incorrect duckdb version?

Besides that, DuckDB extensions can be sensitive to extensions built with a different toolchain. For this reason we recommend using Extensions built with the same toolchain as the DuckDB binary. To achieve this the recommended workflow is:
- clone extension from extension template
- use extension repository to build and test extension
- use extension template CI to build extension binaries
- distribute the extension binaries built from the extension template CI, not the ones you build locally

Hey @reporter, please be aware that this in an issue tracker to an open-source project. Response times are not guaranteed. If you need response time guarantees, you are welcome to take a look [here](https://duckdblabs.com/support/)  where you get a contract with DuckDB Labs to get a private issue tracker and guaranteed response times. 

> Also no instructions there, anywhere I can get it?

The instructions are in the README of the extension template, yes they are a little limited right now, but they should suffice if  you follow the steps correctly.

What you are trying to achieve here is an unsupported path to extension development which we do not offer support for. You are welcome to try and get this to work, but we can not really help you with that. If you want to build DuckDB extensions you should follow the instructions of the extension template, which means to let GitHub actions CI build your binaries, and use those binaries from your DuckDB distribution.

I will close this issue now as this is not really going anywhere.
